newsitem.title: THAILAND: Firm Thai rice prices sideline buyers-trade.
newsitem.headline: Firm Thai rice prices sideline buyers-trade.

text.p: The Thai rice market was quiet this week as activity was subdued by high rice prices which sidelined buyers, trade sources said on Thursday.
Lower-than-expected supplies and high demand for rice for deliveries caused the benchmark 100 percent B grade rice to firm further to US$380-400 per tonne FOB Bangkok.
Fragrant rice 100 percent grade also rose to $620-630 per tonne on the same basis while some offered as high as $640 compared with $620-625 last week.
Traders said they expected the price to be steady or even ease from now as loading activities were at a slower pace and buyers stayed out of the market.
"It should not be much higher than this. It already hard to find buyers at these levels," said one exporter.
Another trader said the spread between Vietnamese benchmark five percent and Thai 100 percent grade had widened to US$100 per tonnes from $40 normally.
But other grades such as parboiled and lower grade rice were mostly stable on slow demand, trade sources said.

At ports, around 11 vessels were loading 75,800 of rice, mostly for Asian destinations. Thailand has shipped 190,075 tonnes of rice between January 1-15 compared with 265,212 tonnes during the same period last year, according to the commerce ministry. --Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642
